title: P02 extension: optimize the token embedding (emb.weight) with Muon too, so every matrix is on Muon
description: P02 (Muon): move the untied 99x256 token embedding emb.weight from pretraining AdamW into the existing split-QKV Muon group (same LR 0.01 schedule, momentum, decay), so every 2D parameter is on Muon and AdamW keeps only biases and LayerNorm vectors; everything else is exactly 064-claude. Muon on hidden matrices was this loop's largest downstream gain and moving the readout into it did no harm (064, +6), and an orthogonalized embedding update moves all 99 input-token directions at equal spectral magnitude, so rarely seen tokens (high line-index citations reached mainly through the ref-shift augmentation, rarer rule names) get input codes as well formed as frequent ones, which should help expert iteration compose citations in >=7-line proofs.
hypothesis: Under AdamW the embedding's updates are dominated by frequent tokens (common rules, low line indices), so its singular spectrum is peaky and rare-token input codes stay close to their random init; Muon equalizes the update across singular directions, giving more separated input codes for rare tokens and one shared update geometry for the input and output token interfaces. If rare-token input codes limit how the model handles citations and longer proof states, round-1 RL sample accuracy on >=7-line targets should rise and compound through the four EI rounds. Counter-risks: an embedding is a lookup table whose natural geometry is per-row, not spectral (the Muon authors keep embeddings on AdamW); the peak per-element update RMS falls from ~1e-3 (AdamW) to ~6.25e-4 (0.01 * 1/sqrt(256) for a full-rank 99x256 orthogonal update), which may under-train frequent rows; and the frozen RL AdamW then fine-tunes an embedding with different geometry. The downstream metric decides.
expected_delta: -30 to +20 theorems at >=7 (central ~-3); final val loss within +-0.004 of 064 (0.091-0.095); steps within 3% of 064's 2339-2354 (one extra 99x256 Newton-Schulz per step); totals 900-1000 s

arch.change: none versus 064-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on every 2D parameter (hidden matrices, token embedding emb.weight, output readout head.weight) throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary on biases and LayerNorm parameters

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, emb (99,256) 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: Every parameter with ndim == 2: all 20 hidden projection matrices (4 per block x 5 blocks), emb.weight (99,256; vocab 99) and head.weight (99,256; no bias): 22 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2, emb and head are orthogonalized whole. emb and head are wide (99<256) so they are not transposed and each update has up to 99 singular values near 1; rows of emb.weight whose token is absent from a batch get no fresh-gradient update (zero rows stay zero under Newton-Schulz) but keep momentum and decay.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; no 2D parameter enters pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction; emb.weight and head.weight therefore keep the same per-step multiplicative decay they had under AdamW.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 064: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. No init change in this experiment; per-seed initial weights and data order bitwise identical to 064.
